messages:
maria: Heads up — I'm prototyping a 'release_epoch' field for rollout metadata. Idea: a monotonic, control-plane-issued epoch token per model family to help clients prefer newer model sets during cross-region failovers and gradual rollouts. Thoughts?

zach: I like the idea of an explicit ordering token, but we need to be careful about semantics. Is this a global ordering or per-model-family? How do we treat concurrent updates? :thinking: 

maria: It's per-model-family (logical name), not wall-clock. Control plane increments the epoch on a release commit. Minimal resolver check would be: prefer highest epoch compatible variant unless an explicit pin exists. Example metadata snippet: 
```
rollout: {
  release_epoch: 42,
  variant: \"v2.1\",
  soft_grace_sec: 300
}
```
Should be cheap for clients to check.

ana: How does this interact with explicit tenant pins and 'leases'? If a tenant pins an older model hash, the resolver should respect that. We need clear precedence rules.

ryan: Proposed precedence: explicit pin > tenant lease (hard lease) > release_epoch semantics (only used when no explicit affinity) > default resolver. Also add a "soft_grace_sec" so clients accept a new epoch for N seconds during transition to avoid flapping.
maria: Exactly. Also want telemetry labels emitted at the resolver level: release_epoch, epoch_transition_start, epoch_transition_end, chosen_precedence. That will help tie quality/regression alerts to epoch boundaries.

ops-bot: deploy: rollout metadata update applied to model-catalog in prod at 2026-03-22T14:12:03Z :rocket: 

zach: One more compatibility note — older clients should ignore unknown fields. We should publish a minimal resolver contract: if release_epoch present and client advertises support, use it; else fallback to current behavior. Document expected resolver API surface (fields and precedence).

ana: Strong suggestion — add a schema-level 'grace_policy' enum: ["soft", "hard", "sticky"] to avoid ad-hoc semantics. 'soft' = ephemeral acceptance window, 'hard' = immediate enforcement, 'sticky' = keep old variant for pinned tenants for a longer TTL.

maria: I'll draft an RFC follow-up with the schema + migration plan (incl. client compatibility matrix and unit tests). I'll also open a small feature-flag rollout so infra can gate it per region. Thanks all :thumbsup:

zach: sgtm. When you draft, include a unit test matrix (pin vs lease vs epoch vs grace policy) — I can help wire the harness.
